title: They survived 9/11; 25 years later, their bonds remain unbroken
gist: National Geographic's documentary miniseries '9/11: Reunited' revisits survivor stories for the 25th anniversary, premiering on linear TV before moving to Disney+ and Hulu the next day; this is a culture/media piece with essentially no investable signal.

insights.claim: National Geographic's three-episode documentary '9/11: Reunited,' produced in collaboration with the 9/11 Memorial and Museum, premieres August 21, 2026 on National Geographic and becomes available on Disney+ and Hulu the following day, reflecting a linear-to-streaming release cadence for prestige documentary content around Disney's owned platforms.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Minimal direct investable signal; notable mainly as a data point on Disney's day-after linear-to-streaming release strategy for prestige documentary content across its owned platforms.
insights.locator: 9/11: Reunited premieres August 21 on National Geographic

insights.claim: Director Julian Jones' prior 9/11 documentary, 2021's Emmy-winning '9/11: One Day in America,' built relationships and trust with survivors that were instrumental in securing their participation in this follow-up series.
insights.speaker: Jennifer Ouellette
insights.so_what: Illustrates how a documentary franchise can compound subject-access advantages over successive productions, a minor production-strategy observation with little market relevance.
insights.locator: it helped that there were pre-existing relationships with many of the survivors
